## Wenyon-backed sandboxes (two-stage contract)

Wenyon dataset mounting is supported only through a template created with the
exact Provider value `volcengine-openkruise`. Template creation stores the
dataset descriptor; it does **not** create a lease and does not need a Wenyon
JWT. A Wenyon template is always private (`visibility=2`), has `replicas=0`,
cannot be shared, and cannot have prewarmed sandbox instances.

The current template API does not echo a Wenyon-backed acknowledgement, so the
CLI cannot preflight-prove that an arbitrary existing template has the
descriptor. Use only a template created in a known supported environment, heed
the CLI warning, and verify the configured mount after the first create. Do not
guess from the template name or treat dry-run as server capability proof.

```bash
# Stage 1: descriptor only; no Wenyon JWT is read or sent.
bohr sandbox template create wenyon-work \
  --image <immutable-image> \
  --sku-name <sku> \
  --provider volcengine-openkruise \
  --wenyon-dataset-id <dataset-id> \
  --wenyon-mount-path /mnt/wenyon \
  --visibility 2 \
  -o json

# Stage 2: the secret/session must already export WENYON_USER_JWT; do not
# substitute BOHR_ACCESS_KEY.
REQUEST_ID="$(uuidgen)"
bohr sandbox create wenyon-work \
  --wenyon-user-token-env WENYON_USER_JWT \
  --request-id "$REQUEST_ID" \
  --yes -o json

# Save canonical data.sandbox_id as SANDBOX_ID (data.sandboxID is the retained
# compatibility spelling), then verify the actual mount.
bohr sandbox exec "$SANDBOX_ID" \
  'test -d /mnt/wenyon && (findmnt -T /mnt/wenyon || grep " /mnt/wenyon " /proc/mounts) && df -hT /mnt/wenyon'
```

The mounted write directory is initially empty. A write lease does **not**
copy or seed the dataset's existing current version. Wenyon prewarm/read-open
only serves read/warm replicas and never populates this write mount. If old
content must survive into the new version, the user or workflow must obtain it
through a separate Wenyon read flow and explicitly copy/write it into the
mount before the Sandbox terminates. The current `bohr sandbox` Wenyon flow
does not support a read lease; stop and say so instead of inventing one.

`--wenyon-user-token-env` accepts only the name of the environment variable
holding the Wenyon/Vouch user JWT. Sandbox create does not implicitly read the
stored Vouch login. Do not populate this variable from `bohr auth token` when
that command reports `auth_method=access_key`; `--as user` does not turn an
AccessKey into a Vouch JWT. The token is request-scoped: it must not
enter the create body, Sandbox metadata, environment metadata, dry-run, logs,
or command output. Dataset ID, mount path, PVC, PFS, and lease details also do
not belong in the Stage 2 body; they come from the template and service.

`sandbox create --timeout 43200` controls the Sandbox's 12-hour lifetime. It
is **not** an HTTP or Wenyon readiness timeout. Do not increase it to work
around write-mount initialization, and do not invent an async create or
client-side lease poll. Template image states `PREPARING`, `READY`, and
`DEGRADED` describe image preparation only. Even image `READY` does not prove
that the Wenyon dataset or PVC is Ready, and a separate prewarm/read-open does
not change the empty-write-mount contract.

Wenyon creates a write lease for each Sandbox. Reuse the same stable request
ID while reconciling one logical create. Validation/auth errors are not
transient; fix the named Provider, mount, or token source before trying again.
If create returns `sandbox_create_outcome_uncertain`, list/reconcile by request
ID instead of blind-retrying create, so a late success is not duplicated. Do
not mistake the expected empty write mount for a readiness failure or retry
create to obtain the current version.

Deleting a Wenyon-backed Sandbox needs no Wenyon JWT. Once an active Sandbox
really reaches `Stopped`, `Deleted`, or `Failed`, the service performs
`finalize -> end` with its machine token and submits the write mount as the new
current version; a create that failed before becoming active is ended without
finalize. There is no discard/end-only CLI for an active Sandbox, and
`sandbox delete --force` only skips the process pre-check: it does not discard
pending Wenyon writes or suppress finalization. Retrieve outputs first, then
use the normal `bohr sandbox delete` flow.

## Mount a Wenyon dataset in an instance

Use an ordinary compute template. The dataset, mount path, mode, and starting
version are **sandbox create parameters**, not template defaults. Check
`bohr sandbox create --help` and the local
[lifecycle reference](references/sandbox/lifecycle.md#mount-a-wenyon-dataset-in-an-instance).

```bash
bohr sandbox create sdbxagent \
  --wenyon-dataset-id <dataset-id> \
  --wenyon-mount-path /mnt/wenyon \
  --wenyon-mode read --wenyon-version current \
  --wenyon-user-token-env WENYON_USER_JWT \
  --request-id "$REQUEST_ID" --yes -o json
```

`read/current` is the default and pins the current version when the lease is
created. `write/current` or a positive version preloads that complete baseline;
only `write/none` starts empty. Missing versions and failed preload do not fall
back to an empty directory. Confirm the dataset, mount path, requested/resolved
version, and actual access mode in the response and verify the mounted data.

`--wenyon-user-token-env` names an existing environment variable holding a
Wenyon/Vouch user JWT; it never takes a token literal. AccessKey authentication
and `--as user` do not supply this JWT. Do not copy `bohr auth token` output when
it reports `auth_method=access_key`. Keep tokens out of command arguments,
metadata, dry-run output, logs, and chat. Do not combine this mount with
`--inherit-auth`.

A writable mount requires an explicit settlement choice: `sandbox delete
--commit --wait` publishes the entire workspace, including deletions;
`--discard --wait` discards it. `--force` only skips the process check and does
not choose settlement. Check the returned `produced_version` after commit.
Without `--wait`, acceptance is not evidence that the data was saved.

If writable execution fails or expires and the workspace remains available,
inspect `recovery_deadline` and choose settlement during the one-hour
`awaiting_decision` window. The write lock remains held; after the deadline the
workspace is discarded. Upstream eviction can make recovery unavailable sooner.
Keep the same request ID while reconciling an uncertain create instead of
creating another instance. A sandbox lifetime limit is not an HTTP or mount
readiness timeout, and an image `READY` state does not prove dataset readiness.
